newsitem.title: SPAIN: Nobel laureate tried to stop ETA killing in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Nobel laureate tried to stop ETA killing in Spain.

text.p: Argentine Nobel peace laureate Adolfo Perez Esquivel said he had contacted a leader of the Basque guerrilla group ETA last week to try to stop the killing of a young town councillor, a Spanish news agency reported.

Esquivel, who has mediated in the past between the separatists and the government, told Europa Press agency late on Monday he had spoken directly with an ETA leader to plead for the life of Miguel Angel Blanco. Blanco was killed on Saturday.

"He did not give any type of assurance about the situation," Esquivel was quoted as saying. "What he told me was they were going to consider what I had requested but they could not assure me of anything."
Blanco's kidnap on Thursday and killing two days later set off three days of massive street demonstrations across Spain.

The 29-year-old low-ranking official of the ruling Popular Party was shot twice in the head after the government rejected ETA's demand to immediately transfer some 500 inmates scattered around the country to prisons in the autonomous Basque region.

Esquivel, who won the Nobel prize for his 1970s human rights work in Argentina, was used by ETA as a mediator to start talks with the former Socialist government in 1995. The initiative fizzled as Spain's March 1996 election approached.

ETA launched a violent campaign for an independent state 29 years ago under Spanish dictator Francisco Franco who repressed any expression of Basque nationalism. After Franco's death, there was a transition to democracy but ETA continued fighting.
The group has killed more than 800 people.
